statement.p: Compute the length of the curve {\bf r\it(t)} = 4 t {\bf \, i} + 2 t {\bf \, j} +(t^2 - 5){\bf \, k} over the interval 0 \le t \le 6.
HINT: use the formula \int \sqrt{ t^2 + a^2} \, dt = \frac{1}{2} t \sqrt{t^2+a^2} + \frac{1}{2} a^2 \ln \left( t + \sqrt{t^2+a^2} \right) + C

static.solution:
\bf r\it(t) is \bf r\it'(t)=4 {\bf \, i}+2{\bf \, j}+2t{\bf \, k}.Using the Arc Length Formula we get: L = \int_0^{6} \left||\bf r\it'(t)\right||\,dt =\int_0^{6} \sqrt{{4}^2+{2}^2+(2t)^2}\,dt =\int_0^{6}\sqrt{4t^2+20}\,dt We substitute u=2t, \,du=2\,dt and use the given integration formula. This gives: L=\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{12}\sqrt{u^2+20}\,du= \left.\frac{1}{4}u\sqrt{u^2+20}+\frac{1}{4}\cdot 20\ln\left(u+\sqrt{u^2+20}\right)\right|_0^{12}=
\frac{1}{4}12\sqrt{{12}^2+20}+\frac{20}{4}\ln\left(12+\sqrt{{12}^2+20}\right) - \frac{20}{4}\ln\sqrt{20}
=\frac{6}{2}\sqrt{164}+\frac{20}{4}\ln\left(12+\sqrt{164}\right) - \frac{20}{4}\ln\sqrt{20}=
\frac{6}{2}\sqrt{164}+\frac{20}{4}\ln\frac{12+\sqrt{164}}{\sqrt{20}} \approx 46.98
